examples.requirement: The vehicle's onboard diagnostic system must perform regular checks for the operational integrity of pedal redundancy features during startup and operation
Power steering systems, whether hydraulic or electronic, must operate effectively in a wide range of environmental conditions, including extreme temperatures
Yaw control systems must compensate for vehicle yaw during adverse driving conditions such as understeer or oversteer
The engine control must transition into a limp-home mode restricting engine output if throttle position sensors within the system detect a fault lasting more than 200 milliseconds.
The vehicle system shall verify successful engagement of the EPB after each parking brake application and notify the driver of any anomalies.

The system shall be designed so that single errors and single errors in combination with latent errors lead to controllable system reactions. The corresponding signal paths (sensors, actuators, functions) shall be monitored.

responses.requirement: The traction control system shall respond correctly to wheel speed sensor inputs under all driving conditions to prevent wheel slip

In cases of conflicting inputs from failed actuators (e.g., unintended throttle and braking), the system prioritizes braking to ensure vehicle deceleration.
The system must continuously calibrate the steering angle sensor to ensure accuracy despite environmental and operational variations
The engine fuel and ignition systems shall autonomously reduce power output to idle conditions in the event of communication loss with the main control unit.
The Anti-lock Braking System (ABS) must reliably receive accurate wheel speed information under all environmental conditions
The system must continuously monitor the yaw rate sensor and detect any failures within [specific time] milliseconds, initiating a predefined safe state operation

Faults in the engine that result in loss of power shall trigger the system to activate hazard lights and alert nearby vehicles.

The system must detect yaw rate with high fidelity to ensure effective input for vehicle dynamics control systems

The ABS and ESC systems must detect a wheel speed sensing failure and activate a fail-safe mode, maintaining as much functionality as possible
Emergency stop mechanisms shall be triggered within 0.1 seconds of dual (throttle and brake) failures to prevent uncontrollable vehicle acceleration.

The system must continually ensure that the throttle position correlates in real-time with the depressed level of the accelerator pedal

The system must detect any Steering Angle Sensor malfunction and report Diagnostic Trouble Codes (DTCs) to the vehicle’s diagnostic system promptly

The system must alert the driver and engage stability control measures if angular velocity sensing exceeds safe operational limits as defined by vehicle dynamics parameters
In cases of conflicting inputs from failed actuators (e.g., unintended throttle and braking), the system prioritizes braking to ensure vehicle deceleration.

Vehicle telemetry systems must incorporate yaw rate sensor data to support advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS) and automated driving functions
In case of wheel steering sensor failure, the system must revert to a fail-safe mode that allows for controlled and safe vehicle operation

The vehicle's steering  must be consistent with the driver's torque sensing on the steering wheel, with no uncommanded delays or discrepancies

The system must guide the vehicle to the nearest safe stop zone in the event of a comprehensive failure impacting multiple systems.

The steering system must remain operable within safe limits in the event of a torque sensor failure

steering system assistance should be consistent across different steering angle sensing and not impair the driver's ability to perform smooth cornering maneuvers

The system must include error correction algorithms to minimize any discrepancy in the steering feedback provided to the driver

ESC systems must use steering torque data to effectively compensate for oversteer or understeer, enhancing vehicle stability

The system must log historical wheel speed data to assist in fault diagnosis and predictive maintenance
Vehicle acceleration must be linear and proportional to the displacement of the accelerattion sensing to provide a smooth and controlled driving experience

The system shall gradually reduce engine power by no more than 20% initially and progressively reach a safe power level within 5 seconds if fuel injector faults persist, ensuring a controlled stop if necessary
Safety systems must continuously monitor yaw rate to identify potential loss of control or rollover risks
Engine system shall limit the throttle-angle for an applicable time if the current vehicle acceleration is higher than the target vehicle acceleration.

The system must be able to identify a fault in the steering torque sensor and transition to a safe state without compromising vehicle control
If brake pressure verification fails to meet command criteria, the system must limit vehicle speed and provide driver notification.
The system shall generate a Diagnostic Trouble Code (DTC) when a wheel speed sensor malfunction is detected
On detecting stepper motor faults, the system shall disable automatic lane change functionality immediately, requiring manual verification by the driver before proceeding.

The vehicle control systems must have the ability to mitigate the effects of erroneous steering and acceleration sensing by the driver, either through system intervention or by providing corrective feedback to the driver
The system must alert the driver to safety-critical conditions related to steering torque sensing, such as malfunctions or deviations from expected performance
If the throttle fails, the system shall immediately reduce throttle opening to achieve engine idle position and provide driver notification through the instrument panel.

Continuous monitoring of the accelerator pedal's displacement shall be conducted to detect any discrepancies indicative of potential faults

The steering system must transfer the braking sensing with minimal torsional deflection to ensure accurate steering angle
